correctness.rationale: The weighted product u v^{delta/(s+delta)} has a derivative depending only on u. On the northwestern saddle stable branch this yields integrable d(log H)/dV ~ (e-B)/[(s+delta)V^2]. Strictly cooperative planar flow and a negative Dulac divergence yield the global one-threshold classification. Rational exact identity and numerical separatrix tests support, but do not replace, the proof. The 3x3 parameter tests and exact 2187 cancellations returned VERIFY_OK 2292. Parameter boundary and nonhyperbolic cases are excluded. The claimed V-interval is the complete graph of the northwest saddle stable branch.

originality.rationale: Primary preprint arXiv:2310.10558v1 contains the printed nonlinear-dispersal ODE, equilibrium and saddle classifications, numerical bistable phase portraits, saddle-node and extinction results. It does not state the quantitative all-large-donor basin graph, universal fractional-power threshold or first correction; this is a new analytical determination beyond a qualitative separatrix. A related earlier critical \(e=B\) claim does not imply the strictly bistable \(e>B\) theorem. Related linear-dispersal and general balance-manifold results do not imply the nonlinear exponent. No result found in targeted published-finding corpus searches dominates the statement. This is best-knowledge originality, not a priority guarantee.
residual_risks: The revised publisher article full body was not materially available in the web text view; a late-added equivalent cannot be excluded.
Unindexed earlier studies of bistable cooperative ecological systems may already derive equivalent regular-variation laws.
Numerical phase portraits in the original demonstrate qualitative basins; only their global quantified theorem and asymptotics are claimed as distinguishing contribution.

value.rationale: The donor-to-recipient founding-density relationship is a natural management invariant of a fragmented habitat. The theorem upgrades qualitative bistable phase portrait to a global threshold and quantifies diminishing returns as donor density grows. A finite positive amplitude, dispersal-determined power and first correction are meaningful structural information not determined by local stability tables.
